caption: The drawing depicts two views of a single ceramic jug set against a plain, off-white background. Both views show the jug in a muted beige or tan color, with a shiny, glazed surface effect. The left view displays the front of the jug, revealing the words “WEST TROY POTTERY” and the number '6' impressed into the upper part of the body. Below the text, there is a blue-painted decorative motif of a bird perched amid stylized blue swirl designs. The right view shows the jug from an angle that includes the handle, which is attached to the jug's upper section, curving outward and downward. The interior of the jug is depicted as darker brown, indicating depth. In both depictions, the jug has a wide, flared opening with a pouring spout, and the artist has detailed highlights and shadows to give a sense of three-dimensionality. The overall composition is centered, with both views occupying the middle of the drawing space.
title: Pitcher
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
